newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice prices seen up on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice prices seen up on foreign buying.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are expected to rise on increased foreign buying, driven mainly by a climb in demand from Iraq, dealers said on Thursday. "We expect a rise in prices and demand from abroad," an official of the state-run Rice Export Corporation said.

The Corporation, which sold 42,016 tonnes of IRRI-6 variety rice in an open auction at $238 per tonne CIF on Tuesday, is likely to stop exports that will now be handled by private sector, the official said.
Rice exports rose to 116,980 tonnes or $35 million worth in November from October's 73,593 tonnes, worth $25 million.
The official said domestic rice prices closed mixed.
